History sensitivity is not established as a predictor of accuracy gains in the studies located. Stronger evidence comes from controlled baselines: [Petrov et al. (2026)](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) compare last-item Markov models, additive history models with recency weights, and SASRec/eSASRec under identical splits and evaluation. History-aware pairwise models outperform last-item controls on all five datasets and both Transformers on four; confidence intervals are absent. This establishes useful earlier-history information, but does not show that perturbation sensitivity predicts improvement or that joint history interactions explain gains.

For this diagnostic, the necessary next step is prospective validation: fix perturbations and proposed interventions beforehand; compare each intervention against the baseline on identical users and candidate sets; relate initial sensitivity to subsequent per-user HR@10 changes, with paired uncertainty estimates and category-specific results. Include last-item-only and additive-history controls to distinguish recency dependence from useful contextual modelling. These are recommended controls, not findings demonstrated by the cited study. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. Keep the pinned 99-negative benchmark for selection; use a small, fixed full-catalog validation audit to assess whether conclusions transfer to simulator recommendations.

Adaptive validation reuse can itself overfit: [Dwork et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629) provide formal safeguards through reusable-holdout mechanisms. Within this fixed benchmark, practical precautions are a preregistered shortlist, capped validation queries, complete trial accounting, and untouched final evaluation; these reduce exposure without guaranteeing validity. Assessment: sensitivity merits exploratory status and a cheap, bounded pilot; a high potential rating or substantial GPU allocation requires demonstrated prediction of paired accuracy gains.
